title: Three Findings, Two Lines
scopeNote: This keeps the two-slope model, the three theoretical patterns and the movable observation window. The crossover and both slopes are fixed and only the window moves, so every change in the reported finding is a change in what was sampled. Independent control of the crossover, the slopes and the window width, and the exercise in predicting what each theory implies before seeing data, stay in the longer version.
summary: Two straight lines that never move, and a window that does. Sampled at the adverse end they show a vulnerability, at the supportive end an advantage, and across the middle both at once.
learningObjectives: Distinguish diathesis-stress, differential susceptibility and vantage sensitivity by their patterns.
Explain how the sampled range decides which of them a study appears to find.
Explain why an accurate description of a window is not a finding about the phenomenon.
Recognise that range restriction does not announce itself in the data.
Say what a paper reporting an interaction should report about its range.
interactionTypes: a judgement about what a restricted study supports
a live control over which part of the environmental range was sampled
two lines drawn across the whole range, faint where the study did not look
a live verdict naming whichever pattern the window supports
a guided toggle between one slice and the whole range
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. Nothing is asked about the learner and nothing is inferred about anybody.
dataStatus: No gene is named and no genotype appears: the grouping variable is a fictional sensitivity score, and the two groups are two halves of a continuum rather than two kinds of person. No disorder, diagnosis or clinical risk estimate is used, the outcome axis is an unnamed standardised outcome, and no figure corresponds to any published finding.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout, with the sampled range on a native range input whose output reads as words rather than a number. The verdict is stated in words in a readout tile alongside the two gaps that produce it, so the figure is never the only route to the finding. Both groups are labelled by name at the ends of their lines, the axis ends are labelled in words, the measured window is shaded as well as marked by line weight, and the chart description gives the window, both gaps, the pattern name and the fact that the lines continue outside it. Nothing is timed and there is no motion.
simulationNotes: The outcome is a slope times the distance from the crossover, with the higher-sensitivity group given the steeper slope, so it does worse at the adverse end and better at the supportive end and the two lines cross in the middle. The pattern a study would report follows from the sign of the gap between the groups at the two edges of its window and nothing else: negative at both edges is diathesis-stress, changing sign inside the window is differential susceptibility, positive at both edges is vantage sensitivity. With the window width fixed, the control reaches all three, and each is a correct description of its own window. Two choices in the drawing carry the argument. The lines are drawn across the whole range at every setting, faint outside the window, because a real study cannot see its own faint stretch and drawing only the window would have concealed it just as effectively. And the scatter comes from one fixed set of residuals scaled in place, so moving the control slides a window over a fixed dataset rather than recruiting new people each time; fresh draws would make the picture jump and the learner would be watching noise. Deliberate simplifications, stated in the caution: both lines are perfectly straight, there is no confounding and little error, and the crossover and slopes are fixed. Real data are messier and the three accounts are genuinely hard to separate, so the demonstration is about what a restricted range can do and not evidence that any published finding is an artefact.
readmeTopic: why the same interaction supports three different theories depending on where you looked
